parallel.requirements: Recognized the C++ task as a Rust 2021 std-only reimplementation requiring matching CLI defaults, first-argument parsing, exact stdout, Cargo structure, root test1.rs, and no external crates.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite proactive multi-agent mode being enabled, the root agent owned all work directly: behavior probing, parser design, file creation, build, verification, and final delivery.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a Cargo package with cli, persistent_vector, and program modules; test1.rs delegates to the library, parse_i32_prefix mimics std::stoi prefix parsing and abort messages, and the vector size loop returns zero for negative n.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Created Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, src/cli.rs, src/persistent_vector.rs, src/program.rs, and /output/test1.rs, built release artifacts, and copied the release binary to /output/test1.
parallel.verification: Ran cargo test --release, cargo build --release, and direct comparisons against the C++ executable for normal, prefix, whitespace/sign, invalid, and out-of-range cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is evidenced at closure; the current official evaluator passed all 38 testcases.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, same-CLI, exact-output, Cargo package, root test1.rs, and compiled executable requirements, including std::stoi edge cases.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single serial root agent owned discovery, implementation, repair, verification, and delivery, with no delegation or child handoff.
serial.implementation: Implemented a Cargo package with app, cli, and persistent_vector modules; test1.rs uses path modules so plain rustc also works, and the parser handles defaults, prefixes, whitespace, signs, invalid input, and out-of-range aborts.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Created the package files, fixed a generic Default compile error in persistent_vector.rs, removed the warning, built /output/test1 with rustc, and built /output/target/release/test1 with Cargo.
serial.verification: Ran cargo test, cargo build --release, rustc --edition=2021 test1.rs -o test1, normal-output comparisons, and abort-path comparisons for abc and 2147483648.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect behavior is evidenced at closure; the current official evaluator passed all 38 testcases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required Rust 2021 std-only Cargo project, root test1.rs entry, CLI default and first argument semantics, exact stdout, and black-box behavior matching.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and followed the same prompt requirements, including std::env::args parsing, std-only implementation, Cargo layout, root test1.rs, and exact output matching.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference is visible; both attempts used the same prompt and both discovered the non-obvious std::stoi prefix and abort behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode was available, but the actual plan assigned inspection, implementation, and verification to the root agent through a local todo list and no child work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a root-agent plan with four local steps covering inspection, Cargo layout, parser/vector implementation, and verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The work decomposition was effectively the same single-owner strategy; the parallel run differed only by having multi-agent enabled without using it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The root agent kept context locally and chose a cli/persistent_vector/program module interface, with no child brief, handoff, or cross-agent contract.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The root agent kept context locally and chose app/cli/persistent_vector modules, including a root test1.rs arrangement intended to work with both Cargo and plain rustc.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no cross-agent context transfer to compare; interface differences were local module-layout choices and both remained coherent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Cargo.toml, root test1.rs, and library modules for CLI parsing, persistent vector behavior, and program logic, then passed its first recorded release tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote a Cargo.toml, root test1.rs, and modules for app, CLI, and persistent vector behavior, then repaired a Default-bound compile error before final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the same functional behavior; serial had a local compile-repair iteration while parallel's recorded build path succeeded after the initial patch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All implementation and verification results stayed in the root trajectory and were finalized in the root final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: All implementation, repair, and verification results stayed in the serial root trajectory and were finalized in the root final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No child result lifecycle existed in either mode; both delivered completed artifacts and a final summary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated its own files into /output and artifact validation found the expected entry file, modules, Cargo files, release binary, and copied executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated its own files into /output and artifact validation found the expected entry file, modules, Cargo files, release binary, debug artifacts, and copied executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used a single writer for final state, so no cross-agent collision, overwrite, leakage, or provenance ambiguity occurred.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran release tests, built the release binary, copied the executable, checked normal and edge behaviors against the C++ executable, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran unit tests, both build modes, normal-output comparisons, abort-path comparisons, and official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's verification was broader because it also built via plain rustc before finalizing; both nevertheless satisfied official acceptance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout in about 130 agent seconds and 160 cell seconds, with no fan-out and no child budget pressure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished without timeout in about 179 agent seconds and 211 cell seconds, with no delegation and one repaired local compile issue.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel-mode run was shorter, but because it did not actually use child agents, the time difference is not evidence of a coordination pattern.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both attempts passed the current completed official evaluation with 38 of 38 testcases. The parallel-mode run did not execute a child-agent or multi-agent mechanism, so its successful solution is best treated as another single-agent implementation rather than a coordinated parallel attempt.

Root agent created a complete Cargo project and delivered both release and copied executables.
serial_contributors: Root agent located the actual source and executable, probed normal and failure behaviors, and implemented a parser matching those observations.
Root agent repaired its compile error, built with Cargo and rustc, and ran reference comparisons before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used cli, persistent_vector, and program modules; serial used app, cli, and persistent_vector modules.
Serial encountered and fixed a generic Default compile issue; parallel did not record that compile-repair step.
Serial performed an additional plain rustc build verification before finalizing.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; both official runs passed and no actual parallel coordination occurred
